q: למרפאה מגיע מטופל בן 76 הסובל מירידה קוגניטיבית מזה כ- 3 שנים. מדווח על ירידה בזיכרון ובהתמצאות בזמן. אשתו מדווחת כי במהלך השנה האחרונה הירידה הקוגניטיבית מביאה לקושי גובר בניהול פעולות אותן היה מבצע היטב עד כה (קניות, נהיגה, עבודה על המחשב, ניהול הטיפול התרופתי, אחזקת בית וכו'). בבדיקת MMSE מתקבל ציון של 24/30. מה הטיפול התרופתי המומלץ במטופל זה ומדוע?
o: היות ומדובר ב- MCI מומלץ טיפול במעכבי כולין אסטרז שנמצאו יעילים בעיכוב התקדמות מ- MCI למחלת אלצהיימר
מומלץ טיפול ב Memantine, אשר מאושר לשימוש למחלת אלצהיימר בדרגה קלה-בינונית ומאט את קצב הירידה במבחן MMSE
מומלץ טיפול במעכבי כולין אסטרז בחולי אלצהיימר, שכן הוא גורם להאטה של ההחמרה הקוגניטיבית ולשיפור באיכות חיים
מומלץ שילוב של מעכב כולינאסטרז ו- Memantine כיוון שהוכח כי במחלת אלצהיימר בדרגה קלה השילוב יעיל יותר מכל אחת מהתרופות בנפרד בשימור תפקוד
explanation:
Progressive cognitive decline that now impairs shopping, medication management and other previously independent tasks supports a dementia syndrome. **If evaluation identifies Alzheimer dementia or another suitable subtype, offer a cholinesterase inhibitor for modest symptomatic benefit.** An MMSE of 24 and this history do not, by themselves, identify the cause or prove disease modification.

**A. Treat MCI to prevent conversion.** Loss of independent everyday function argues beyond MCI. Cholinesterase inhibitors have not reliably prevented conversion of MCI to Alzheimer dementia.
**B. Memantine for mild disease.** Its established indication is moderate-to-severe Alzheimer dementia. His current functional history suggests an earlier stage.
**C. Offer a cholinesterase inhibitor for Alzheimer dementia.** Discuss the small average cognitive and functional benefits, adverse effects and goals. An individual improvement in quality of life is not assured.
**D. Combine both drugs in mild dementia.** Additional functional benefit from routine memantine add-on in mild disease has not been demonstrated.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 895–896, 910–911.

. Offer a cholinesterase inhibitor for Alzheimer dementia.** Discuss the small average cognitive and functional benefits, adverse effects and goals. An individual improvement in quality of life is not assured.
. Combine both drugs in mild dementia.** Additional functional benefit from routine memantine add-on in mild disease has not been demonstrated.

q: בת 85, הסובלת מסרטן גרורתי ודמנציה מתקדמת הוכרזה כחולה נוטה למות שאינה כשירה. בברור רצונה נמצא כי תוקף ייפוי הכוח עליו חתמה ובו מינתה את שכנתה, פג לפני שנתיים, אך לאחרונה מונה לה אפוטרופוס מטעם המדינה. מי צריך להיות מקבל ההחלטה בעניין הטיפול בסוף החיים?
o: האפוטרופוס
אחייניתה שהינה קרובת המשפחה היחידה שלה
הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם השכנה
הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם האפוטרופוס
explanation:
ייפוי כוח לסוף החיים שפג תוקפו אינו מקנה עוד לשכנה סמכות מחייבת. עם זאת, המסמך והעדות של אדם שהכיר היטב את החולה עשויים לסייע בבירור רצונה.
**הרופא האחראי יעיין במסמך, יברר עם השכנה את רצון החולה ואת טיב הקשר ביניהן, ויכריע לפי המסלול החל.**

**א. האפוטרופוס מחליט** מינוי מטעם המדינה אינו מעניק מאליו מעמד של אדם קרוב המכיר את רצונה של החולה.
**ב. האחיינית מחליטה** קרבת משפחה לבדה אינה הופכת אותה לנציגת החולה לפי חוק זה.
**ג. הרופא האחראי והשכנה** עצם בחירתה הקודמת מצדיקה לברר מה ידוע לה. כשהיא עונה להגדרת אדם קרוב, ניתן לשקול את הצהרתה המפורשת במסלול הקבוע בחוק.
**ד. הרופא והאפוטרופוס** בהיעדר הצהרת אדם קרוב אפשר לשקול עמדת אפוטרופוס שהוא עצמו אדם קרוב. מינויו לאחרונה אינו מוכיח היכרות כזאת.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 3, 5(ג), 9, 39(ב).

q: After removal of a urinary catheter, a woman cannot empty her bladder and has a residual volume of 600 mL. Which action matches Hazzard's bladder-retraining protocol?
o: Give a bladder relaxant and attempt voiding later in the day
Lengthen the intervals between voiding attempts to train the bladder
Reinsert a Foley catheter; retry voiding in a few days
Wait for urodynamic testing before arranging drainage of the bladder
explanation:
A voiding trial checks whether the bladder can empty after catheter removal. **Drain the 600 mL residual with a Foley and plan another trial in a few days.**

**A. Give a bladder relaxant and attempt voiding later in the day** — A relaxant may further suppress detrusor contraction.
**B. Lengthen the intervals between voiding attempts to train the bladder** — Waiting longer lets an already overfilled bladder distend further.
**C. Reinsert a Foley catheter; retry voiding in a few days** — The protocol advises a Foley when residual urine exceeds 300 to 400 mL.
**D. Wait for urodynamic testing before arranging drainage of the bladder** — Formal pressure testing can follow if needed. The bladder needs drainage now.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, p. 711, Table 47-11.

. Reinsert a Foley catheter; retry voiding in a few days** — The protocol advises a Foley when residual urine exceeds 300 to 400 mL.
. Wait for urodynamic testing before arranging drainage of the bladder** — Formal pressure testing can follow if needed. The bladder needs drainage now.

q: An 83-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities is considering sacral neuromodulation for urgency incontinence that has not improved with treatment. Which statement accurately describes this intervention?
o: Treatment is delivered through repeated needle stimulation near the ankle
Cure rates are lower in older adults with multiple comorbidities
Treatment is delivered by botulinum toxin injection into the bladder wall
The procedure primarily corrects mechanical leakage during exertion
explanation:
Sacral neuromodulation uses an implanted pulse generator and sacral leads to treat refractory urgency. **It can be effective in older adults, although cure rates are lower with older age and multiple comorbidities.**

**A. Treatment is delivered through repeated needle stimulation near the ankle** — Ankle stimulation describes percutaneous tibial nerve treatment.
**B. Cure rates are lower in older adults with multiple comorbidities** — Age and comorbidity affect the expected chance of cure and belong in counseling.
**C. Treatment is delivered by botulinum toxin injection into the bladder wall** — Bladder-wall injections deliver botulinum toxin, a different procedure.
**D. The procedure primarily corrects mechanical leakage during exertion** — The indication here is refractory urgency, while exertional leakage usually reflects outlet weakness.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, pp. 714–715.

. Cure rates are lower in older adults with multiple comorbidities** — Age and comorbidity affect the expected chance of cure and belong in counseling.
. Treatment is delivered by botulinum toxin injection into the bladder wall** — Bladder-wall injections deliver botulinum toxin, a different procedure.
. The procedure primarily corrects mechanical leakage during exertion** — The indication here is refractory urgency, while exertional leakage usually reflects outlet weakness.

q: An older patient asks to start caloric restriction after hearing that CALERIE slowed the advancement of physiologic age. What principle should guide interpretation before an individual recommendation?
o: Infer dementia prevention from the marker response.
Look for clinical benefit and harms beyond the marker.
Infer suitability for malnutrition from the marker response.
Use the marker as a proxy for treatment safety.
explanation:
A change in a physiological aging measure is a surrogate finding. **Assess clinical effectiveness and safety before recommending caloric restriction to an individual**, particularly when nutritional reserve may be limited.

**A. Infer dementia prevention from the marker response** — Slower change in an aging measure is not a demonstrated cognitive outcome.
**B. Look for clinical benefit and harms beyond the marker** — Ask whether people function better or avoid disease and whether restriction causes harm in the relevant population.
**C. Infer suitability for malnutrition from the marker response** — Further energy restriction could worsen weight and muscle loss. A biomarker result cannot answer that safety question.
**D. Use the marker as a proxy for treatment safety** — Favorable laboratory changes can coexist with clinical harms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 602.

. Infer suitability for malnutrition from the marker response** — Further energy restriction could worsen weight and muscle loss. A biomarker result cannot answer that safety question.
. Use the marker as a proxy for treatment safety** — Favorable laboratory changes can coexist with clinical harms.

q: An 83-year-old woman develops hyponatremia after diuretic treatment. Evaluation confirms hypovolemic hyponatremia with volume depletion, no congestion, and no life-threatening neurological symptoms. Which treatment principle matches her volume status?
o: Restrict water and increase a loop diuretic to treat congestion.
Replace volume with isotonic saline and monitor serum sodium.
Give hypertonic saline to treat established SIADH.
Observe for spontaneous correction based on dilute urine.
explanation:
Volume depletion stimulates antidiuretic hormone and promotes water retention despite low serum sodium. **Replace volume with isotonic saline and monitor serum sodium** in this patient without severe neurologic symptoms.

**A. Fluid restriction and loop diuresis.** That approach targets congestion and would aggravate her volume deficit.
**B. Isotonic saline.** Restoring circulation can switch off the stimulus to water retention. Sodium may then rise quickly.
**C. Hypertonic saline for SIADH.** The specified cause is hypovolemia, and no life-threatening neurologic manifestation is present.
**D. Wait for dilute urine.** She has documented volume depletion requiring treatment. Spontaneous water diuresis cannot be assumed.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 587.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: גבר בן 85 נמצא ביום 3 של שיקום אקוטי לאחר החלפת שני ברכיים. יש לו CKD stage 3 (eGFR 45), CHF (EF 40%), ואוסטאופורוזיס. הוא מוטיבציה אך מפתח כאב קשה (9/10) עם כיפוף הברך מעבר ל-70 מעלות, המגביל את התקדמות הטיפול. טיפול אנלגטי נוכחי: acetaminophen 1g TID, celecoxib 200mg יומי, oxycodone 5mg q6h PRN (משתמש ב-3-4 מנות ביום). אשתו שואלת על תרופות כאב חזקות יותר. מהי ההתאמה המתאימה ביותר?
o: להעלות oxycodone ל-7.5mg q6h PRN
להוסיף gabapentin 100mg TID
להחליף celecoxib ב-naproxen 250mg BID
להוסיף tramadol 25mg q6h
explanation:
Pain on postoperative knee flexion calls for reassessment of the joint, the timing of analgesia and the patient's function. **The description supplies no neuropathic features that would justify routinely adding gabapentin to oxycodone.**

**A. Raise oxycodone** More oxycodone may impair alertness or breathing. Reassess benefit, timing and toxicity before increasing.
**B. Add gabapentin** Gabapentin needs renal adjustment and can amplify opioid sedation. A neuropathic indication would change the discussion.
**C. Switch to naproxen** Naproxen remains a systemic NSAID. Kidney disease and heart failure increase concern about renal injury and fluid retention.
**D. Add tramadol** Adding tramadol duplicates opioid exposure and adds serotonergic and seizure risks.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1060–1065. AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Tables 5–6.

q: A 77-year-old woman with recurrent falls takes amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. Which adverse-effect profile explains the concern about its use in older adults in the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Cholinergic stimulation with bradycardia and increased secretions.
Anticholinergic effects, sedation and orthostatic hypotension.
Dopamine blockade with rigidity and postural instability.
Sympathetic stimulation with tremor and sustained hypertension.
explanation:
Amitriptyline can impair thinking and alertness and lower blood pressure on standing. Together these effects are particularly hazardous in a patient with recurrent falls.

**The relevant combination is anticholinergic activity, sedation, and orthostatic hypotension.** All three can occur even when the indication is neuropathic pain.

**A. Cholinergic stimulation with bradycardia and increased secretions** — Amitriptyline inhibits muscarinic signaling rather than producing cholinergic secretions.
**B. Anticholinergic effects, sedation and orthostatic hypotension** — The combination of anticholinergic effects, sedation and orthostatic hypotension increases fall risk.
**C. Dopamine blockade with rigidity and postural instability** — A dopamine-blocking antipsychotic is a more typical cause of drug-induced rigidity.
**D. Sympathetic stimulation with tremor and sustained hypertension** — Sustained adrenergic hypertension is not the characteristic Beers adverse-effect profile.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2059.

. Dopamine blockade with rigidity and postural instability** — A dopamine-blocking antipsychotic is a more typical cause of drug-induced rigidity.
. Sympathetic stimulation with tremor and sustained hypertension** — Sustained adrenergic hypertension is not the characteristic Beers adverse-effect profile.

q: A 76-year-old man with stage 3b chronic kidney disease (eGFR 42 mL/min/1.73 m²) and diabetes has asymptomatic bacteriuria with 100,000 CFU/mL of E. coli discovered during preoperative evaluation for cataract surgery. Urinalysis shows 10–20 WBC per high-power field and no nitrites. He has no dysuria, urgency, or fever. Which management approach fits Hazzard?
o: Prescribe a course of ciprofloxacin.
Prescribe a course of nitrofurantoin.
Withhold antimicrobial treatment.
Postpone cataract surgery pending a negative culture.
explanation:
Asymptomatic bacteriuria before nonurologic surgery is not an indication for antibiotic treatment. **Withhold antibiotics before cataract surgery** in this man without urinary symptoms or systemic illness.

**A. Prescribe a course of ciprofloxacin** — Eradicating a urine isolate has no demonstrated perioperative benefit in this setting.
**B. Prescribe a course of nitrofurantoin** — There is no symptomatic cystitis to treat. Pyuria does not change that.
**C. Withhold antimicrobial treatment** — The exception for selected urologic procedures involving mucosal trauma does not apply to cataract surgery.
**D. Postpone cataract surgery pending a negative culture** — A sterile urine culture is not a prerequisite for this nonurologic procedure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1702.

. Withhold antimicrobial treatment** — The exception for selected urologic procedures involving mucosal trauma does not apply to cataract surgery.

q: Before treatment for lung cancer, grip strength is found to be below the reference values for sex and population. How should this finding be interpreted in the evaluation of sarcopenia?
o: It supports attributing weakness to sarcopenia before considering other causes
It supports postponing intervention until muscle mass measurement is complete
It supports suspicion of sarcopenia and assessment and treatment of weakness
It supports postponing intervention until impaired gait speed is also present
explanation:
A dynamometer measures how much force the patient produces. A low value can reflect muscle disease, hand pain, neurologic disease or the circumstances of testing. **Suspect sarcopenia, investigate other causes and address the weakness.**

**A. Attribute weakness to sarcopenia first** A grip result identifies a deficit but cannot distinguish its cause. Check for limitations such as painful hand joints or neurologic impairment.
**B. Wait for a muscle-mass measurement** Low grip predicts adverse outcomes in its own right. Assessment and appropriate treatment can begin before confirmation.
**C. Evaluate and act on the low strength** Weakness warrants attention during cancer care, including review of mobility, nutritional status and potential contributors to the abnormal test.
**D. Wait for gait impairment** EWGSOP2 uses poor physical performance to grade severity. It is not a prerequisite for intervening on low strength.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 732, 735–736.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA

q: בן 70, מזה כשלוש שנים פגיעה קשה ביציבות, מלווה בנפילות חוזרות., בנוסף מציין. הפרעה בדיבור ובבליעה בבדיקתו: אורטוסטטיזם משמעותי, ללא עדות לרעד, כוח גס תקין, החזרים מאד ערים, הליכה. לא יציבה על בסיס רחב. במהלך הבדיקה סבל מאירוע של סטרידור. מהי האבחנה הסבירה ביותר?
o: VASCULAR DEMENTIA
MULTIPLE SYSTEM ATROPHY - CERBELLAR
PARKINSON'S DISEASE
HUNTINGTON CHOREA
explanation:
Cerebellar gait ataxia with severe autonomic failure strongly favors **multiple system atrophy, cerebellar type (MSA-C)**. Dysarthria, dysphagia, brisk reflexes and inspiratory stridor reinforce that diagnosis.

**A. Vascular dementia.** Cognitive and cerebrovascular findings would be central. Stridor and this autonomic-cerebellar combination point elsewhere.
**B. MSA-C.** Degeneration affects cerebellar and autonomic pathways. Laryngeal dysfunction can produce stridor.
**C. Parkinson disease.** Typical early Parkinson disease produces bradykinesia and rigidity. Marked early orthostasis and cerebellar ataxia are warning signs.
**D. Huntington disease.** Chorea and behavioral or cognitive changes are more characteristic.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 985–986 and 993.

. Parkinson disease.** Typical early Parkinson disease produces bradykinesia and rigidity. Marked early orthostasis and cerebellar ataxia are warning signs.

q: Well-formed visual hallucinations of children or furry animals early in a cognitive illness most suggest which condition?
o: Alzheimer disease in its mild stage
Dementia with Lewy bodies
A medial temporal seizure focus
Schizophrenia with tactile hallucinations
explanation:
Hallucinations occur in many neurologic disorders and may be formed or unformed. **Well-formed visual hallucinations such as children or furry animals are a prominent early sign of dementia with Lewy bodies.**

**A. Alzheimer disease in its mild stage.** Less well-formed visual hallucinations occur in the moderate to severe stages of Alzheimer disease.
**B. Dementia with Lewy bodies.** The book's early sign of dementia with Lewy bodies.
**C. A medial temporal seizure focus.** Medial temporal lesions and seizures are linked with gustatory or olfactory hallucinations.
**D. Schizophrenia with tactile hallucinations.** Tactile hallucinations are linked with schizophrenia, affective disorders or drugs, not this visual pattern.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 141.
